question.problem: Solve the linear congruence $5x≡4\,(\text{mod}\,6)$ using trial and error.
question.worked_solution:
Since the modulus $n=6$ is fairly small, we can solve the congruence by trial and error. 

Substituting $x=0,1,2,3,4,5$ into the congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}5\cdot 0 & ≡0≢4 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & \times  \\ 5\cdot 1 & ≡5≢4 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & \times  \\ 5\cdot 2 & ≡10≡6+4≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & ✓ \\ 5\cdot 3 & ≡15≡2\cdot 6+3≡3≢4 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & \times  \\ 5\cdot 4 & ≡20≡3\cdot 6+2≡2≢4 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & \times  \\ 5\cdot 5 & ≡25≡4\cdot 6+1≡1≢4 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & \times \end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the solution is $x≡2\,(\text{mod}\,6).$

**Note**: Any number congruent to $2$ modulo $6$ is a solution. For example, note that $8≡2,$ and this also satisfies our congruence:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x & ≡5\cdot 8\, &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡40\, &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡6\cdot 6+4\, &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡0+4\, &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡4\,\,✓\, &  & (\text{mod}\,6)\end{aligned}
$$
